title: Mechanism of Smilax china L. in the treatment of intrauterine adhesions based on network pharmacology, molecular docking and experimental validation.
authors: Shi, Tingting; Hou, Chuqi; Duan, Yongzhen; Li, Yuliang; Liu, Wenqin; Huang, Peixian; Zhou, Yuhua; Yu, Shanshan; Song, Luyao
one_liner_zh: 该文用网络药理学和分子对接研究中药菝葜治疗宫腔粘连的机制，虽含分子对接但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Smilax china L. (SCL) is a traditional herbal medicine for the potential treatment of intrauterine adhesion (IUA). However, the mechanisms of action have not yet been determined. In this study, we explored the effects and mechanisms of SCL in IUA by network pharmacology, molecular docking and molecular biology experiments. METHODS: Active ingredients and targets of SCL were acquired from TCMSP and SwissTargetPrediction. IUA-related targets were collected from the GeneCards, DisGeNET, OMIM and TTD databases. A protein‒protein interaction (PPI) network was constructed by Cytoscape 3.9.1 and analysed with CytoHubba and CytoNCA to identify the core targets. The DAVID tool was used for GO and KEGG enrichment analyses. Furthermore, molecular docking was employed to assess the interaction between the compounds and key targets. Finally, the mechanisms and targets of SCL in IUA were verified by cellular experiments and western blot. RESULTS: A total of 196 targets of SCL were identified, among which 93 were related to IUA. Topological and KEGG analyses results identified 15 core targets that were involved in multiple pathways, such as inflammation, apoptosis, and PI3K/AKT signalling pathways. Molecular docking results showed that the active compounds had good binding to the core targets. In vitro experiments showed that astilbin (AST), a major component of SCL, significantly reduced TGF-beta-induced overexpression of fibronectin (FN), activation of the PI3K/AKT signalling pathway and the expression of downstream factors (NF-kappaB and BCL2) in human endometrial stromal cells, suggesting that AST ameliorates IUA by mediating the PI3K/AKT/NF-kappaB and BCL2 proteins. CONCLUSIONS: AST, a major component of SCL, may be a potential therapeutic agent for IUA. Moreover, its mechanism is strongly associated with regulation of the PI3K/AKT signalling pathway and the downstream NF-kappaB and BCL2 proteins. This study will provide new strategies that utilize AST for the treatment of IUA.
abstract_zh: 背景：菝葜（Smilax china L.，SCL）是一种传统草药，可能用于治疗宫腔粘连（intrauterine adhesion，IUA）。然而，其作用机制尚未明确。在本研究中，我们通过网络药理学、分子对接和分子生物学实验探讨了SCL在IUA中的作用及机制。方法：从TCMSP和SwissTargetPrediction获取SCL的活性成分及靶点。从GeneCards、DisGeNET、OMIM和TTD数据库收集IUA相关靶点。利用Cytoscape 3.9.1构建蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络，并通过CytoHubba和CytoNCA分析以识别核心靶点。使用DAVID工具进行GO和KEGG富集分析。此外，采用分子对接评估化合物与关键靶点之间的相互作用。最后，通过细胞实验和蛋白质印迹验证SCL在IUA中的机制和靶点。结果：共鉴定出SCL的196个靶点，其中93个与IUA相关。拓扑分析和KEGG分析结果确定了15个核心靶点，这些靶点涉及多种通路，如炎症、凋亡和PI3K/AKT信号通路。分子对接结果显示，活性化合物与核心靶点具有良好的结合能力。体外实验表明，SCL的主要成分落新妇苷（astilbin，AST）显著降低了转化生长因子-β（TGF-β）诱导的人子宫内膜基质细胞中纤连蛋白（FN）的过表达、PI3K/AKT信号通路的激活以及下游因子（NF-kappaB和BCL2）的表达，提示AST通过介导PI3K/AKT/NF-kappaB和BCL2蛋白改善IUA。结论：AST作为SCL的主要成分，可能是IUA的潜在治疗药物。此外，其机制与调节PI3K/AKT信号通路及下游NF-kappaB和BCL2蛋白密切相关。本研究将为利用AST治疗IUA提供新策略。
